Kittle's 77.3 rec yards/game clears 54.5 on form, but that is average-chasing into SEA's best zone (middle 4.79 YPA), so it is not an edge. Evans 54.7 vs a 50.5 line is explosive-dependent (260 air yards, 6.3 yards/target) against a defense with 5 explosives allowed. Purdy 32.0 rush yards/game on 8.0 YPC (12 carries) looks fluky and is not used.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Samuel cleared 34.5 because the 34.5 line was the market fading a quiet three-game sample — one designed crosser plus YAC, or a quiet Evans, pushed him to 5 catches and 45 yards the L3 role never showed. JSN stayed under 95.5 because 11.6 yards per target was the fluke: SEA led, Wilson took 20-plus carries, SF sat on the intermediate, and 9 targets at 8 yards each landed near 72. That clock-kill flip is the real counter on JSN, which is why it stays a lean; it is not stronger than Samuel's 15-yard usage gap, so the under stays.
slip_story: Base-script concentration slip, not a shootout and not a clock-kill stack: SEA's throws stay on JSN (over 95.5) while SF's throws stay on Evans/Kittle/McCaffrey and Deebo's receiving line is too high (under 34.5). Both lose together only if flip 1 hits (SEA lead, clock drain, manufactured Deebo touches). Do not add Kittle or Evans overs — those need the explosive flip this SEA defense (5/135) has not allowed. No TDs, one market per player.
